Definition: from G435 and ὤψ (the countenance; from G3700); man-faced, i.e. a human being:--certain, man.
BiblicalUsage: Man, the human being, man-faced, made in God's image and fallen from it. The first man Adam brought sin into the world, the second man Christ brings life, and every man will give account for the deeds done in the body. The word runs the whole length of the Bible, from the man formed of the dust to the man who will judge the world.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe man is the Bible's great subject because God made him for Himself: dust that God breathed into, a sinner Christ died for, and a creature who will stand before his Maker. Adam's fall and Christ's life are both told in this one word, and I hold that no man is beyond the reach of the second Adam.
RelatedEvents: The Temptation in the Wilderness; The Fall
